name: quick-phrases-field
title: Quick phrases field
description: A textarea with one-tap phrases underneath, such as Leave at the door or Ring twice: tap to add, tap again to take it out, typing stays free.
docs: value and onValueChange speak the whole text as a plain string; defaultValue starts it uncontrolled. phrases is a list of strings or { id, text } (use ids when the same words appear twice or the text is translated). A tap adds the phrase behind the text after separator (a line break by default, or ", ", ". " or " " to keep one sentence going, or two line breaks to keep paragraphs apart, where taking a phrase out takes its gap with it; a phrase that ends its own sentence with a full stop, exclamation mark or question mark is not given a second full stop), and a second tap takes it out again together with its separator. A long phrase wraps inside its chip instead of being cut off, and on a touch screen the chips are taller so a thumb can hit them. A phrase counts as present when it stands as a piece of its own between the separators, whatever the capitals and with or without a closing full stop, so typing it by hand presses its chip too. maxLength is the textarea's own limit and also disables any chip that would not fit, with a line under the chips saying how many need more room than is left; a chip that is already in the text can always be removed. Every add and remove is announced politely (Added Leave at the door). label names the field (hideLabel keeps it for assistive technology), phrasesLabel renames the small heading over the chips, name posts the text, and labels renames the announcements and the lines about the limit. The pure helpers addPhrase, removePhrase and locate live in quick-phrases-field/phrases.
